setting: Southern border of a Cossack sloboda at the edge of the Wild Fields, a scorching dry midsummer of 1553: endless feather-grass steppe with kurgans and stone babas, an oak forest in a ravine where woodcutters fell timber for boats, a river behind the hill, and the sloboda of whitewashed thatched clay huts with wattle fences, wells with sweeps, cattle and sheep.

characters.dmytro: 27-year-old Cossack border rider, tall and long-limbed, long tanned face with high cheekbones, shaved head with a black forelock, black drooping mustache, no beard, coarse brown wool svytka over a linen shirt, red sharovary, blue sash, yellow boots, shablia
characters.dmytro_horse: dappled grey steppe horse with a dark mane and tail
characters.patrol_elder: 45-year-old thickset Cossack, grey-streaked mustache, grey sheepskin kalpak, faded green zhupan, dark blue sharovary, samopal on his back
characters.patrol_young: 19-year-old slim freckled Cossack, short fair hair, thin blond mustache, white linen shirt, grey svyta, blue sharovary
characters.forest_workers: Cossack woodcutters in sweat-soaked linen shirts with rolled sleeves and sharovary, forelocks, axes and two-man saws
characters.starosta: 60-year-old sloboda elder, white forelock, long white mustache, heavy brown zhupan, green sash, wooden staff
characters.villagers: sloboda villagers of all ages, women in embroidered linen shirts, plakhta skirts and white kerchiefs, old men, boys and girls, wooden buckets and spades

palette: Passages: sepia and graphite on warm ivory paper, fine organic pen and pencil hatching inspired by Abraham van Westerveld. Cover only: ultra-realistic full-color cinematic photograph.
notes: The Tatars who set the fire are never seen; the threat is the fire itself, a wall of black smoke advancing with the wind toward the sloboda. Dmytro rides with two patrol comrades (older and younger). In the DEAD ending Dmytro's right side is burnt: show only soot, singed clothes and a swollen shut right eye, never burn wounds; the dead are hinted at as distant dark shapes in the ash.
cover_palette: bleached straw-gold steppe, hard pale-blue sky turning brown-black with smoke, orange fire light, charcoal-black burnt ground, whitewashed huts; Dmytro's red sharovary and blue sash as accents.
illustration_notes: 16 passage drawings. Tatars are never visible. Fire burns wild vegetation, not the village. The successful village branch preserves every hut. The counterburn leaves a broad black strip. The village firebreak is ploughed by two oxen. In the tragic branch Dmytro has a closed right eye and a fallen grey horse; no graphic injury.
